κινεῖται δίκη· εἴτε τοῦ ἐκ περιτομῆς διὰ Χριστὸν εἰς Θεὸν ἀσεβήσαντος, εἴτε τοῦ

ἐπίσκοπος ἐνθάδε ὠνο μάσθη· ὅτι Θεὸς ἐπίσκοπος εἴρηται, καὶ οἱ ἐπίσκοποι ἐκείνου
τὴν εἰκόνα παντὶ τῷ τρό πῳ φιλοτιμοῦνται, οἱ καλοὶ καὶ ἀγαθοὶ, φο ρεῖν. Καὶ ὥσπερ
ὁ μιμησάμενος εἰκόνα βα σιλικὴν, τιμᾶται ἐπὶ τῷ καλῶς αὐτὴν μι μήσασθαι· τιμᾶται
δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ αὐτὴν κεκοσμηκέναι· οὕτως μακάριος ἐπίσκοπος ὁ νοήσας τὸν

̓Επιστήμη, ἡ περιοχὴ τῶν ὡσαύτως ἐχόντων θεωρία, σύνεσις δὲ ἡ διάκρισις. εʹ.
Πότερον οὐχ ἡ κακία σου ἐστὶ πολλὴ, ἀναρίθμητοι δέ σου εἰσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι; Εἰκότως
οὖν φημὶ οὐχ ἁπλῶς γεγονέναι σε ἄδικον, ἐπεὶ πάσχεις τοιαῦτα, οἷα οὐδεὶς τῶν
κακῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν τούτοις γεγεννῆσθαι, δη λονότι πλείονα κακίαν [τῶν κακῶν] ὑπὲρ
τοὺς ἄλλους ἐσχηκέναι. Κακία ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ κακὴ ἕξις, οἷον λύπης, ὀργῆς, καὶ ἐπι
θυμία ἀπρεπής· ἀμαρτία δὲ ἡ ἐνέργεια· διὸ πρῶτον εἶπεν τὴν κακίαν, εἶτα τὴν ἁμαρ
τίαν, τὴν μὲν πολλὴν, τὰς δὲ ἀναριθμήτους. Πάνυ πολλοὺς ὁρῶ ἁμαρτωλοὺς, καὶ
οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν τηλικούτοις περιπέπτωκεν οἷος σύ. 370 Εἰκὸς γὰρ, διὰ τὸ ἀναρίθμητόν
σου τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων καὶ τὸ πλῆθός σου τῶν πταισ μάτων, ταῦτά σοι
ἐπεληλυθέναι. ʹ. Ἠνεχύραζες δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου διακε νῆς· ἀμφίασιν δὲ γυμνῶν
ἀφείλου. Πρόσχωμεν, οἱ τοκογλύφοι· μήποτε ἐνε χυράζωμεν διακενῆς. Ὠφέλιμα τὰ

γινομένων ἐν ἀν θρώποις. Ὑπολαμβάνει τοῦτο ὁ Ἐλίφας περὶ τοῦ Ἰὼβ, ἐπειδὴ ᾔδει
αὐτὸν πλούσιον, καὶ ὑπώπτευσεν ἀπὸ τοιούτων τινῶν πόρων πλου τεῖν αὐτόν· διό
φησιν· Ἠνεχύραζες διακενῆς, τουτέστιν μηδὲν ἐποφειλόμενος. –Εἰ δὲ ἐδάνεισα, καὶ
μὴ πιστεύων τῷ δανεισαμένῳ, ἔλαβον ἐνήχυρον ἀξιόχρεων πρὸς ὃ ἔχρησα, ἔλαβον
ἐνήχυρον, οὐ διακενῆς δέ. Εἰ μέντοι, συκοφαντῶν αὐτὸν, καὶ λέγων ὀφείλειν μοι μὴ
δυνάμενον ἀποδοῦναι, ἀπαιτῶ καὶ λαμ βάνω, ἐνήχυρον [λαμβάνω] διακενῆς.
Προσεπιτείνει δὲ πάλιν, ἄλλην αὐτοῦ ἁ μαρτίαν οἰόμενος γεγονέναι. Ἔστι ποτὲ λα
βεῖν ἀμφιάσματα, οὐ τοῦ γυμνοῦ, ἀλλὰ πλου σίου, ἔχοντος ἕτερα ἀποκείμενα
ἐνδύματα πολλὰ λαβεῖν, τρία δή· ὧν τῶν πολλῶν ἐκεῖ ἔλαβον ἀμφίασιν· ἄλλα
γυμνοῦ, ἄλλα πλου σίου. Ἐὰν μέντοι γε χιτῶνα ἔχῃ τις ἕνα, καὶ τοῦτον τὸν χιτῶνα,
προφάσει τοῦ ἀπαι τεῖν τὸ ἐμὸν, ἐκδύσω, μὴ ἐλεήσας ἐκεῖνον τὸν γυμνὸν, ἀμφίασιν
τοῦ γυμνοῦ ἀφειλόμην. Πολλὰ δὲ τοιαῦτα ἐν ἡμῖν γίνεται, ὅταν δανείζωμεν, ὅταν
πρὸς ὀφειλέτας ἐρχώμεθα· πολλάκις ὀφειλέτης ἡμῶν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν πέ νεται, μὴ

pass_a_gloss: of him to walk [around]... For they are in ignorance; for the light burst forth from themselves, about whom he was saying: I am the light of the world. k. Unburning fire fell upon him. And according to the hidden [thing], unburning fire is, that is, that which is according to conscience, or even that which lies in future righteous judgments. And as if by fire, he says, he shall be consumed, so that he may say: Not even a burial is worthy of him. k. This is the portion of an impious man from the Lord, and a possession of those belonging to him from the bishop. By which divine justice moves against him; whether of the one who through circumcision via Christ was impious toward God, or of the paradoxical, or however an impious person may be, the declared portion is to him. – Learn who the bishop here was named; for God is said to be bishop, and the bishops of Him imitate the icon in every way, the good and the noble ones, to strive. And just as one having imitated a royal icon is honored for having imitated it well; and he is honored also for having adorned it; thus is the blessed bishop who has understood the true bishop, and zealously follows him, and becoming as God among men, or the one having a bishop who makes him truly a bishop in Christ Jesus, to whom is the glory and the power unto the ages of the ages. Amen. Cap. 41, 11, 12. And their children play, taking up a psaltery and a lyre, and they rejoice with the voice of a psalm. Behold, even their foolish children play for themselves. For they themselves say psalms of Valentinus and hymns of Basileidus, and they utter certain things, rejoicing with the voice of a psalm. Cap. 22, 2. Whether is not the Lord the one teaching understanding and knowledge? Let us see what Eliphaz says toward the righteous; whether etc... This, having been spoken by Job, Eliphaz also rushes to the word, and says: I also know that the words, through which one indeed being impious is straightened, but the other is punished, God alone is wise; and I know this also, that God indeed, as you himself said, is the giver of good things; but evil gives the punishments. – The doctrine is healthy... – Knowledge is the comprehension of those having such a theory, and understanding is the distinction. 5. Whether not... your wickedness is much, and your sins are innumerable?; It is expected then that I say you have become unrighteous not simply, because you suffer such things as no one of the wicked [does], but that you have come to be in these, clearly having had more wickedness than the others. Wickedness is an evil disposition in the soul, such as grief, anger, and an unseemly desire; but sin is the activity; therefore first he said the wickedness, then the sin, the one being much, the others being innumerable. I see very many sinners, and none of them has fallen into such great things as you. For it is likely, because of your innumerable sins and your multitude of faults, that these things have happened to you. You were defrauding the brothers by lending; and you were depriving them of the clothing of the naked. Let us pay attention, O engravers; let us not ever defraud by lending. The words are useful, according to this it is to speak sins truthfully according to reason, as they occur among men. Eliphaz supposes this concerning Job, because he knew him to be rich, and he suspected from such things that he might be wealthy through certain means; therefore he says: You were defrauding by lending, that is, not leaving anything unpaid. –If indeed I lent, and not believing in the one lent to, they took a pledge of worthy value for what I used, they took a pledge, and not by lending. But if, slandering him, and saying he is unable to pay what he owes me, I demand and take, I take a pledge by lending. And he adds again, supposing another of his sins to have happened. It is possible at times to take garments, not of the naked, but of the rich, having other clothes lying around, many, three indeed; of these many, they took clothing; some of the naked, some of the rich. But if indeed one has a single tunic, and this tunic, he makes a pretext to demand my [property], I will strip him, not having pitied that naked man, I deprived him of the clothing of the naked. And many such things happen among us, when we lend, when we come to debtors; often our debtor falls into excess, being unable to pay; and we, having closed up our bowels, become pitiless and harsh, not seeing that a woman feeds and children, and she is barely fed from the few obols provided to him; we demand bitterly, even when having abundance with ourselves. Such things happen in bitter demands, sometimes...
pass_b_english: They wander about in ignorance, for the light has emanated from within themselves, even as He declared: [[quote >> John 8:12 >> I am the light of the world]]. An unconsuming fire shall fall upon him. Regarding the hidden meaning, this unconsuming fire refers either to the conscience or to the judgments that await the righteous in the future. He says that the man shall be consumed by fire so that it may be said he is not even worthy of a burial.

This is the portion assigned to the impious man by the Lord, and it is a possession held by those under the bishop. Through this, divine justice is set in motion against him, whether he is one who, though circumcised, acted impiously toward God through Christ, or whether he is a paradoxical person; regardless, the declared portion belongs to the impious. Consider who the bishop mentioned here was. It is said that God is the Bishop, and the bishops of God strive to imitate His likeness in every way, being good and noble. Just as one who imitates a royal icon is honored for the excellence of his imitation and for the beauty he adds to it, so too is the blessed bishop who has perceived the true Bishop and follows Him with zeal. Such a man becomes like God among men; or, alternatively, he is one who possesses a bishop who truly makes him a bishop in Christ Jesus, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

Their children also play, taking up the psaltery and the lyre, finding joy in the sound of psalmody. Indeed, even their foolish children engage in such play, for they sing the psalms of Valentinus and the hymns of Basileidus, finding delight in the melody of their songs.

Is not the Lord the one who imparts understanding and knowledge? Let us observe what Eliphaz says to the righteous man. After Job has spoken, Eliphaz rushes to join the argument, saying: I also know that God alone is wise, and that through certain words one impious man is corrected while another is punished. I also know that God is the giver of good things, as you have said, whereas evil brings about punishment. This doctrine is healthy. Knowledge is the comprehension of those who possess such a theory, while understanding is the power of distinction.

Is it not possible that your wickedness is great and your sins are beyond counting? It is therefore expected that I should say you have not become unrighteous by mere chance because you suffer such things as no other wicked man does; rather, you have fallen into these circumstances because you possess a greater wickedness than others. Wickedness is an evil disposition of the soul, such as grief, anger, or disordered desire, whereas sin is the actual exercise of that disposition. Therefore, he first mentioned wickedness and then sin—the former being a great state and the latter being innumerable acts. I see many sinners, yet none have fallen into such profound depths as you have. It is probable that because of your countless sins and your multitude of faults, these things have befallen you. You were defrauding your brothers through usury, and you were stripping the naked of their clothing. Let us take heed, O engravers, that we never defraud others through lending. These words are useful, for they allow us to speak truthfully about sins as they occur among men according to reason. Eliphaz assumes this regarding Job because he knew Job was wealthy and suspected he might have acquired his riches through improper means; thus he says: You were defrauding by lending, meaning you left nothing unpaid. If I lend money but, distrusting the borrower, I take a pledge of great value as security, that is not true lending. But if I demand and seize a pledge by lending because I slander him, claiming he cannot pay his debts, then I am lending. He adds another suspected sin: it is possible to take garments not from the naked, but from the rich who have many clothes lying around. Yet, if a man has only a single tunic and I use that as a pretext to demand my property, I strip him; having no pity for the naked man, I have deprived him of his clothing. Many such things occur among us when we lend or visit debtors. Often the debtor falls into such excess that he cannot pay, and we, becoming hardened and pitiless, fail to see that a woman must feed children on the few coins provided, and we demand payment bitterly even when we ourselves live in abundance. Such bitter demands occur...

choices.choice: The gloss uses passive constructions and literal translations of Greek particles (e.g., 'is the portion', 'is the activity'). The rewrite employs active, literary English (e.g., 'divine justice is set in motion', 'sin is the actual exercise') to reflect Origen's theological precision rather than a word-for-word grammatical map.
